title: Recall is not current
lesson: Check a remembered repository instruction against its source revision, then refresh both the stored record and the current context before acting.
limitations: Revision checking and invalidation are illustrative application logic, not automatic store guarantees.
The passing test result is illustrative; no agent integration or real test migration was executed.
Persistent instructions do not enforce tool permissions.
Audio was analysed for levels and cue alignment, not physically listened to.
Self-reviewed; comparative selection and human editorial promotion remain separate.

transcript.text: An approved repository test command at revision r1 is saved, then recalled into session A. Both use npm test.
The repository changes to revision r2 and pnpm test. Saved memory still holds r1. A new session B opens without a command.
Session B recalls the old command successfully. A separately implemented source revision check detects r1 versus r2 and stops the candidate before execution.
The workflow clears the stale record and task candidate, reloads r2 from the repository into saved memory, and supplies r2 to session B.
Session B runs the current command and shows an illustrative passing result, then the picture fades. Correct memory does not guarantee passing tests or enforce permissions.
